title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. His prized pendant eventually came under the possession of a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead encountered Knight Artorias, who had retained only the very last vestige of his sanity in the battle against the Abyss, still desperate to put down the corrupted creatures of Oolacile. During the fight that ensued between him and the Chosen Undead, Artorias succumbed to the Abyss entirely, and was finally defeated by the Undead.

Ciaran, who had arrived at the arena where Artorias was corrupted by the Abyss, also requested the Soul of Artorias from the Chosen Undead who had finally put an end to the knight's suffering, with the intention of paying proper respects to her passed dear friend.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Oolacile -  Dark Souls - location - lead 
 lead : The lost land of **Oolacile** is a location that no longer exists by the events of *Dark Souls*. Several sources allude to its existence centuries beforehand and its focus on sorceries. Dusk of Oolacile states that the land "was reduced to ashes" long ago.

The later version of the game, *Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition*, comes with extra content that takes place in Oolacile 200-300 years before the events of the game, where the Chosen Undead must take the place of Artorias the Abysswalker and rescue Dusk from Manus, Father of the Abyss. During this period, Oolacile is slowly being swallowed by the Abyss. The content was later added as DLC to the console versions of the game as *Artorias of the Abyss*.

title: Four Kings
snippet: A nation of humans freed from the shackles of the Darksign, and who not only began to understand the powers of their Dark Soul but had an entire army at their disposal that shared this power, represented an unparalleled threat to the gods of Anor Londo, who branded the Darkwraiths as diabolical enemies of man and of every living thing. For this reason, Artorias, one of the Four Knights of Gwyn, was sent to fight the soldiers of New Londo and was given a Silver Pendant to deflect the Dark of the Abyss in its magical forms. However this did not prove sufficient to cross the Abyss of the Four Kings, and Artorias was forced to forge a covenant with the "beasts of the Abyss", obtaining a ring that would allow him to cross the Abyss, while also cursing his Greatsword. Artorias thus became known as the "Abysswalker", and hunted the Darkwraiths, but failed to eliminate the Four Kings and thus eliminate the Abyss of New Londo.

snippet:

The Golem will only drop the pendant if Dusk of Oolacile has been rescued from within the Golden Crystal Golem, which can be found in an alcove past the Hydra in Darkroot Basin. It will only drop if the player talked to Dusk after rescuing her or if Dusk was killed.

The pendant can be obtained even if the player has killed the Golem prior to rescuing Dusk.

title: Covenant of Artorias
snippet:
Covenant of Artorias -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : Covenant of Artorias allows the player to reach the Abyss. As such, it is necessary in order to reach the Four Kings boss battle. Without wearing the ring, it is impossible to survive the fall into the Abyss. Taking off the ring during the fight with the Four Kings will cause the player to be devoured by the Abyss. Other than this, the ring has no other purpose.

The Covenant of Artorias is one of the very few rings that do not carry over to NG+; players are required to kill Great Grey Wolf Sif every playthrough to obtain the ring and beat the game. This ring, when dropped, will end up in the chest behind Kingseeker Frampt after the player has quit and reloaded the game. However, in the remaster, it will automatically be in the player’s inventory.

The township has become filled with enemies (specifically Bloatheads, Bloathead Sorcerers, and a Chained Prisoner) as the Abyss spreads, and is seemingly deserted.

One of the Four Knights of Gwyn, Artorias the Abysswalker, arrived in Oolacile to rescue Dusk of Oolacile from Manus, Father of the Abyss, but fell victim to the Abyss. By the time the Chosen Undead found him, Artorias was hostile and engaged them in combat. After the Chosen Undead defeated the brave knight, they finish what Artorias had started, continuing through Oolacile Township and onward, eventually defeating Manus and rescuing Dusk.

title: Abyss
snippet: Knight Artorias famously traversed New Londo's Abyss and hunted the Darkwraiths therein. He was protected by the power of a magical ring, which he gained after making a covenant with the beasts there. The ring prevented him from being swallowed by the void, but it led to his sword becoming cursed. In recognition of his actions, he was awarded one of Anor Londo's treasures, a Silver Pendant that allowed him to repel Dark sorceries; eventually he traveled to Oolacile to combat the threat of Manus, the lord of the Abyss. He ultimately failed in his mission he was overtaken by the dark, leaving behind his companion Sif.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Abyss Watchers were the main component of the Undead Legion of Farron, a special fighting force formed to combat the threat of the Abyss. Taking inspiration from the Wolf Knight (Sir Artorias, the Abysswalker), the Abyss Watchers themselves sought to utilize the techniques of Artorias, and partook of "wolf blood" to do so. Empowered by the legacy of Artorias, they became intensely strong and agile, fighting in a coordinated and sporadic pack akin to wolves.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - artorias_the_abysswalker 
 artorias_the_abysswalker : Artorias had an unbreakable will of steel and his skill with greatswords was unmatched, making him a fierce opponent. Additionally, he was known as the first mortal to traverse the Abyss.

Although Artorias is only scarcely mentioned during the Chosen Undead's journey to the Kiln of the First Flame, he is one of the many obstacles the Chosen Undead encounters in Oolacile. Gravely injured and corrupted by the Abyss by the time he is encountered, Artorias still proves a formidable foe although the Chosen Undead eventually prevails. Hawkeye Gough will thank the player for setting Artorias free with honor.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: As the Abyss continued to spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience from fighting the Abyss and its creatures in New Londo. However, Artorias's silver pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Artorias, together with his trusted companion Sif, nevertheless faced Manus, but his strength proved insufficient to defeat the Father of the Abyss. Wounded in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier to protect Sif against the Dark. Artorias, his soul corrupted by the Abyss and his armor corroded, was left alone in his fight against the Abyssal creatures of Oolacile.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: A nation of humans freed from the shackles of the Darksign, in possession of an army empowered by their boundless Dark Soul, represented an unparalleled threat to the gods of Anor Londo, who branded the Darkwraiths diabolical enemies of man and of every living thing. Artorias, as one of the Four Knights of Gwyn, was sent to fight the dark soldiers of New Londo, being granted a Silver Pendant to deflect the Dark of the Abyss he would face. However this did not prove sufficient to cross into the Abyss of the Four Kings, and Artorias was forced to forge a covenant with the "beasts of the Abyss", obtaining a ring that would allow him to cross the Abyss, but also cursed his sword in the process. Artorias thus became known as the "Abysswalker" and hunted the Darkwraiths, but failed to eliminate the Four Kings and close the Abyss of New Londo. She is found after falling through an illusory floor, and leads the player to an injured but protected Sif. Here the Chosen Undead may choose to secure the white wolf by clearing the area of humanity phantoms, receiving the Cleansing Greatshield as a gift.

Elizabeth pledges to tell future generations that Artorias defeated Manus and halted the Abyss, appearing to confirm that at least part of Artorias' legend was indeed a fabrication, though he was nevertheless a brave and extremely powerful knight.

title: Painted World of Ariamis
snippet:
Painted World of Ariamis -  Dark Souls - location - upgrade_materials 
 upgrade_materials : Dragon Scale

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: As the Abyss spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience with fighting the Abyss and its creatures after the events of New Londo and his hunt for the Darkwraiths, and possessed a Silver Pendant that protected him from the Dark. However, Artorias's pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Together with his trusted companion Sif, Artorias faced Manus but his strength proved insufficient to defeat him, and he succumbed to the Abyss. Injured in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier that protected Sif from the Dark. Now corrupted to his soul by the Abyss and with his armor corroded, Artorias was left to fight alone and hold back the treacherous citizens of Oolacile.

title: Artorias of the Abyss
snippet:
Artorias of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lore 
 lore : Artorias of the Abyss* takes place approximately 200 to 300 years before the events of *Dark Souls*, in the land of Oolacile. It features three of the Four Knights of Gwyn‎. The events of the DLC are also related to the story of *Dark Souls II*, as Nashandra was born from a fragment of Manus' soul.

title: Broken Pendant
snippet:
Broken Pendant -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Half of a broken stone pendant. The vine appears to originate from Oolacile.

A powerful magic can be sensed from this ancient stone. Yet men of this time can neither manipulate nor sense its power, which has a distinct air consisting of both reverence and nostalgia.

title: Dusk of Oolacile
snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : , also known as **Princess Dusk**, is a character and merchant in *Dark Souls*. She is voiced by Emma Pierson, who also voiced Anastacia of Astora.

title: Dusk of Oolacile
snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Dusk appears to believe that she was saved by Artorias, as told by the legend, while in actuality she was saved by the Chosen Undead. While unaware that Artorias had been corrupted by the Abyss before he could save her, Dusk's senses do hint that the Chosen Undead bears the same "resonance" as her fabled savior, leading her to question the details of her temporarily intangible captivity.
The feelings that she sensed during her imprisonment in the Abyss—"*a wrenching nostalgia, a lost joy, an object of obsession, and a sincere hope to reclaim it"—*are evocative of the "shards" of Manus present in Drangleic, who each represented a form of longing; namely Nadalia, Alsanna, Nashandra and Elana.

title: Dusk of Oolacile
snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Dusk is an optional character for the main game; when summoned via her summon sign in Darkroot Basin, she sells the player sorceries from Oolacile as a reward for rescuing her. These include: Hidden Body, Cast Light and Chameleon. Depending on the player's playstyle, it may be well worth the trouble of rescuing her.

While interacting with her is not obligatory for progressing the main storyline, she must be sought out in order to access the *Artorias of the Abyss* DLC.

title: Dusk of Oolacile
snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Dusk is from the ancient and long-dead land of Oolacile, which practiced magic alien even to the magic realm of Vinheim. It is unknown how she was trapped in the Golem in the first place, but it is clear that she is in the wrong era.

title: Dusk of Oolacile
snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : Dusk is trapped inside a Golden Crystal Golem located in an alcove past the Hydra in Darkroot Basin. After defeating the Hydra, players may need to go through a load screen for the golem to spawn.
After killing the golem, Dusk will be available as a summon sign on the lake shore where the player fought the Hydra, next to a tree in front of the Knight Set loot. Reverse hollowing is not required to summon her (her summon sign vanishes after the Chosen Undead obtains the Broken Pendant).
Immediately after Manus, Father of the Abyss is defeated, Dusk appears in the arena and can be spoken to, but will vanish if the player leaves the area. Her summon sign will return as before in Darkroot Basin.

title: Dusk of Oolacile
snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - notes 
 notes : If answered "No" after her introduction, she won't be available to be summoned for the rest of that playthrough.
She does not fight back if attacked.
She drops nothing, and the Dark Hand can steal no liquid Humanity from her.
If the player kills Dusk of Oolacile, Elizabeth will also die.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - rings 
 rings : Each of the Four Knights was gifted a unique ring imbued with special powers. The Chosen Undead can find them scattered throughout Lordran, and their item descriptions give minor insight into who the knights were and what they did.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - hornet_ring 
 hornet_ring : Engraved with a hornet, the Hornet Ring belonged to Lord's Blade Ciaran. Increasing the power of critical attacks, it allows its wearer to lay waste to their foes much like how Ciaran did to Lord Gwyn's enemies.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - lord_s_blade_ciaran 
 lord_s_blade_ciaran : Lord's Blade Ciaran was part of the Lord's Blades, a group of assassins in the employ of Gwyn. Known for her unique porcelain mask and annihilating Gwyn's enemies. The Chosen Undead encounters her grieving in the arena where they fought Artorias.

Sensing the presence of her compatriot's soul, she requests the Chosen Undead to give it to her, so she may pay proper respect to Artorias.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - wolf_ring 
 wolf_ring : Engraved with a howling wolf, the Wolf Ring belonged to Artorias the Abysswalker. Improving the Poise of its wearer, it complemented Artorias' unbendable will.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - hawkeye_gough 
 hawkeye_gough : Hawkeye Gough was the only Giant of the Four Knights, and the leader of the Dragonslayers, the archers that fought the Dragons in the Age of Ancients.

By the time the Chosen Undead meets him, Gough is blind. Upon their first encounter, he thanks the Chosen Undead for slaying Artorias, allowing the corrupted knight to die with his honor intact.

Despite being blind, Gough was still a great sharpshooter. He proves this by shooting Kalameet out of the sky, on the Chosen Undead's request. This allowed the Chosen Undead to fight the dragon on more equal footing, eventually leading to the latter's demise.

Despite his skill, there were archers that rivaled even Gough. One such individual was Pharis , which was especially impressive as Pharis was only human.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - hawk_ring 
 hawk_ring : Engraved with a hawk, the Hawk Ring belonged to Hawkeye Gough. Boosting the range of bows, it allows its wearer to loose arrows as if they were fired from Gough's own greatbow.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : The **Four Knights of Gwyn** were Lord Gwyn's most trusted warriors. Only one knight is encountered in the original console version of *Dark Souls*: Dragon Slayer Ornstein.

The other three knights, Artorias the Abysswalker, Lord's Blade Ciaran and Hawkeye Gough, are only mentioned; Artorias is deceased by the events of the game, and the fates of the other two are left unrevealed, although they are presumed deceased as well.

In the *Artorias of the Abyss* DLC, the player is dragged into the past, allowing them to meet the other three knights in Oolacile.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - leo_ring 
 leo_ring : Engraved with a lion, the Leo Ring belonged to Dragonslayer Ornstein. Boosting the power of counter attacks, it befits Ornstein's skill with his weapon of choice.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet: Artorias' left arm is near useless due to being harshly damaged, presumably while protecting his companion, Sif, the Great Grey Wolf, who fought alongside Artorias in the Abyss. Artorias saved Sif from corruption by using his Greatshield to create a magic barrier around the wolf, shortly before succumbing to the Abyss himself.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - dragonslayer_ornstein 
 dragonslayer_ornstein : Ornstein is believed to be the captain of the Four Knights. He is also the only one who must die by the player's hand in order for the story to progress. It is rumored his spear is powerful enough to cut a giant boulder in two.

It is implied that the Ornstein the Chosen Undead encounters is but a golem, and the real one left Anor Londo to search for the Nameless King. In Dark Souls 3 after encountering the Nameless King boss fight his armor can be found in the boss fight arena on Archdragon Peak implying that he did reach the Nameless King, however, it is not on a corpse, meaning he may have simply left it behind.

title: Golden Scroll
snippet:
Golden Scroll -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Give to Orbeck of Vinheim in Firelink Shrine to upgrade his stock of Sorceries:

title: Golden Scroll
snippet:
Golden Scroll -  Dark Souls III - item - description 
 description : A golden scroll chronicling the vast research of the xanthous scholars.

Give to a sorcerer to learn the arts of Oolacile.

In the lost land of Oolacile, the sorceries orchestrated light, and were said to shine in golden hues.

title: Golden Scroll
snippet:
Golden Scroll -  Dark Souls III - item - lead 
 lead : The **Golden Scroll** is a key item in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Golden Scroll
snippet:
Golden Scroll -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Found in Farron Keep.

From the Keep Ruins bonfire, head toward the main gate and then turn right, following the wall. Once reaching a clearing inhabited by many Basilisks, turn right to find a cave with a corpse holding the scroll, along with a chest containing the Antiquated Set.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Despite this, when returning to the current age and speaking to Dusk, she would simply note that the Chosen Undead looks a lot like Artorias (believing it was Artorias who rescued her from Manus), without expanding on whether or not the Chosen Undead's actions had any effect in saving Oolacile.

While speaking to Marvelous Chester, he would say that "Oolacile has brought the Abyss upon itself [...] Fooled by that toothy serpent, they upturned the grave of primeval man, and incited his ornery wrath", implying that either Kingseeker Frampt or Darkstalker Kaathe had a hand in Oolacile's downfall. Due to the inherent darkness of the Abyss, Darkstalker Kaathe is the more likely culprit.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Oolacile -  Dark Souls - location - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : By the time of *Dark Souls III*, Oolacile, who's name was once lost to time in *Dark Souls II*, is remembered as an ancient lost land and renowned for its "golden sorceries", whose spells of golden hues allowed a caster to produce and manipulate light, and even be capable of reversing time. These pure natured sorceries, even the most elementary of spells, are such that have not been achieved even by the Dragon School of Vinheim.

Those who researched the lost sorceries were known as Xanthous Scholars, and wore yellow clothing with a oversized crown supposedly made in imitation of a divine creature of Oolacile, along with a band of brass medallions with the number of which indicates their success in their research; a point of pride lost on others. Some chose to foolishly imitate the scholars by wearing yellow. The Xanthous Scholars' vast research of Oolacile's light sorceries were recorded on golden scrolls.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Oolacile -  Dark Souls - location - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : During the events of *Dark Souls*, Oolacile is not a location that can be visited. The Enchanted Ember is described as "a vestige of the lost land of Oolacile". Dusk of Oolacile expands more on her home land during dialogue with the Chosen Undead, describing it as "the home of ancient sorceries". She explains that Oolacile's sorceries are more "of an approximation" when compared to those used by the Chosen Undead, but also reveals that she does not belong to this time and that Oolacile "was reduced to ashes" long ago.

The locations of both the Enchanted Ember and Dusk of Oolacile — in Darkroot Garden and Darkroot Basin respectively, as well as the Grave of Artorias located in Sif's boss area — imply that Oolacile was once located nearby. The maps of Darkroot Garden and Royal wood also have striking similarities.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Oolacile -  Dark Souls - location - plot 
 plot : Traveling to the land of Oolacile can only be done after obtaining the Broken Pendant, which is dropped by a Crystal Golem in The Duke's Archives after speaking with Dusk of Oolacile. Approaching the area where Dusk is initially saved, with the Pendant in one's possession, will reveal a shadowy portal, which the player examines.

title: Abyss Attack Dog
snippet:
Abyss Attack Dog -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : They are encountered in an isolated area of the Royal Wood within Oolacile, along the river leading to Black Dragon Kalameet.

title: Abyss Attack Dog
snippet:
Abyss Attack Dog -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Abyss Attack Dogs are similar in appearance and behavior to Attack Dogs.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet:
Unusual for a weapon, the Abyss Greatsword has fairly good magic resistance, although most shields are still preferable.

Like Chaos weapons, the Abyss Greatsword scales with Humanity (up to 10). When fully upgraded, with 10 Humanity, and 40/40 in Strength and Dexterity, the Abyss Greatsword deals the most raw physical damage among all of the Greatsword class weapons, beaten only by ultra greatswords and Great Hammers/Axes in this regard. This damage difference is not significant and when factoring in that Abyss Greatsword cannot be buffed, other weapons are capable of vastly out performing this sword without putting points into two different casting stats.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet:
Abyss Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - scaling_percentages 
 scaling_percentages : ***Strength - 55%**
***Dexterity - 55%**
***Intelligence - 0%**
* **Faith - 0%**

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet: If one does not meet the Intelligence and Faith requirements but still meet the required Strength and Dexterity, they will still be able to do full damage with the sword, but, will get a stagger animation that makes them immune to backstabs. This occurs because since the Intelligence and Faith requirements don't actually affect the damage output, but rather the Strength and Dexterity, they can completely disregard investing to get the Intelligence and Faith stats to 18. However, the drawback to this is that it will not allow one to do any follow ups, as once this sword makes contact, it will bounce off, stopping the user from doing anything for a few seconds.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet:
Abyss Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Compared to its Greatsword of Artorias' true version, the Abyss Greatsword has a distinct moveset, lower stat requirements, weighs one unit less, has a heavily deteriorated appearance, and deals purely physical damage. The strong attacks are reminiscent of those performed by Artorias himself. Despite requiring 18 Faith and Intelligence, the Abyss Greatsword does not scale off of these parameters. This should discourage most builds from utilizing this weapon.

Unusual for a weapon, the Abyss Greatsword has fairly good magic resistance, although most shields are still preferable.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet:
Abyss Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - description 
 description : This greatsword belonged to Lord Gwyn's Knight Artorias, who fell to the abyss.

Swallowed by the Dark with its master, this sword is tainted by the abyss, and now its strength reflects its wielder's humanity.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet:
Abyss Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - availability 
 availability : The Abyss Greatsword is created by ascending any Standard +10 greatsword, ultra greatsword, straight sword (other than the Broken Straight Sword or Straight Sword Hilt) or dagger at the Giant Blacksmith in Anor Londo with the Soul of Artorias and 5,000 souls.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : **Alvina of the Darkroot Wood** (白猫アルヴィナ), commonly referred to as **Alvina**, is a character in *Dark Souls* who acts the leader of the Forest Hunter covenant. She is voiced by Ève Karpf.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Alvina inducts the player into the Forest Hunter covenant when answered "Yes" to both of her initial questions. Answering "No" to her first question will cause her to shun the player. Hurting Alvina in any way will not kill her, but it will cause her to disappear. If the player is in the Forest Hunter covenant, attacking her will also count as a betrayal and the NPCs in the forest will become hostile, including Shiva. It is possible to make Alvina neutral again by absolving sins with Oswald of Carim. Alvina will be present and repeat the covenant dialogue.

Killing one intruder as part of the Forest Hunter covenant will result in Alvina giving the player a Divine Blessing. Killing 3 trespassers of The Forest will grant the Ring of Fog.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : Alvina can be found in Darkroot Garden, in a ruined building past the sealed door that can be opened with the Crest of Artorias. The most direct way to get there is through the sealed door and sticking to the left.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - description 
 description : Alvina appears to be a large cat, resembling a Great Feline but she is also capable of understanding and talking the human language.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Her name and title, accurately translated from the original Japanese description, should be "Alvina, the White Cat" (白猫アルヴィナ).

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Alvina is a white Great Feline that had lived for centuries since the early Age of Fire and is capable of human speech. At one point she became a trusted friend of Knight Artorias, one of the Four Knights of Gwyn, as well as his companion Great Grey Wolf Sif.

After Artorias' death, Alvina moved to the ruins of Oolacile, now overgrown and known as the "Darkroot Garden", where the knight had succumbed in his fight against the Abyss of Manus. Sif too had moved here after he survived the battle with Manus and inherited Artorias' divine greatsword and the magical ring that had allowed the knight to cross into the Abyss. The wolf settled in the forest where Artorias' tomb had been erected and, wielding his companion's sword in his jaws, continued to fight to guard Artorias' rest, slaughtering the numerous Undead intent on plundering the tomb of the legendary knight.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - drops 
 drops : Her drops can only be obtained if Lautrec kills her.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Anastacia strongly resembles the Maiden in Black from *Demon's Souls*: the maiden is an ally to the Slayer of Demons like Anastacia is an ally to the Chosen Undead. Both of them have some physical impairment: the Maiden is blind, and Anastacia is mute. They are also both guardians to sacred places.
It appears that Anastacia is locked in her cell in Firelink Shrine; however, in the prologue, she is seen kneeling over an unnamed undead in the graveyard.
The description of the Blood-Stained Skirt implies that, as well as having her tongue cut out, Anastacia's legs were crippled to keep her from leaving Firelink Shrine. Her model is missing both legs around the knees.
Her name translates from Greek ἀνάστασις as “revived” that closely links to her fate.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : She can be found in a cell below the Firelink Shrine bonfire, down the stairs located to the left of the Crestfallen Warrior.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Initially, she is unable to speak, for her tongue has been removed sometime ago. Nonetheless, the player can still interact with her. As with other Fire Keepers, Anastacia has the ability to reinforce the Estus Flask, in exchange for Fire Keeper Souls.

If Knight Lautrec of Carim is in Firelink Shrine, he will kill Anastacia when either of the following occurs:

The player rings both Bells of Awakening.
The player picks up the Fire Keeper Souls in the Undead Parish and in Blighttown.

While Anastacia is dead the bonfire in Firelink Shrine is inactive and unusable. She leaves behind the Dingy Set and the Black Eye Orb. The Black Eye Orb is an invasion item, allowing players to find and invade Lautrec's world to defeat him and retrieve Anastacia's Fire Keeper Soul.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : **Anastacia of Astora** (アストラのアナスタシア), also known as **The Ash Maiden,** is a Fire Keeper in *Dark Souls*. She keeps the bonfire in Firelink Shrine lit.

Anastacia is voiced by Emma Pierson, who also voiced Dusk of Oolacile.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Anastacia is suggested by herself and at least one other character to be "impure", mainly of speech. However, what exactly made her "unclean" is never revealed, as she tells very little to the player even with her tongue restored. It has been hinted from item descriptions that Anastacia may have chosen her own banishment and even imprisonment.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Returning Anastacia's soul to her cage will revive her, reigniting the Firelink Shrine bonfire. Her speech will also be restored, allowing the player to engage in conversation with her.

Once Anastacia is revived, if the player places the Lordvessel, offers at least one Lord Soul or Lord Soul Shard to it, and then talks to her, she will fully kindle the Firelink Shrine bonfire.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Besides hailing from Astora, little is known about Andre; he seems to cherish dependability, which might vaguely suggest a history of betrayal, though this is never elaborated upon. He is also acquainted with the Giant Blacksmith, as evidenced when he notices the player holding the Giant's Coal.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Andre's stocky build, beard, dour demeanor and profession as a blacksmith of legendary weapons resembles popular depictions of the *dwarves*, originally of Norse myth, and later popularized by the works of Tolkien and *Dungeons & Dragons*.
**Andre's name is similar to that of the dwarf *Andvari* of Norse myth.
**Bodies of blacksmiths closely resembling Andre are found in various locations, seemingly petrified. In Norse myth, dwarves are said to be turned to stone by sunlight. Two of the petrified dwarves in Dark Souls are located in ruined buildings which appear to have been exposed to sunlight due to structural damage.
**Dwarves in Norse myth are famed for the creation of magic items, particularly magic weapons of unparalleled strength. These include Thor's hammer *Mjolnir*, Odin's spear *Gungnir*, the reforged sword *Gram*, and the cursed sword *Tyrfing*.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : Andre of Astora is located directly below the bonfire in the Undead Parish, between Darkroot Garden and Sen's Fortress.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Often the first blacksmith new players come across, Andre of Astora can be a welcome sight. Andre of Astora is the only blacksmith that can ascend weapons down the Standard path from +5 to +6 and from +10 to +11. He is also the only blacksmith that can ascend weapons down the Raw, Divine and Occult paths.

He also sells some basic upgrade materials, as well as many weapons (some of which are unique to him). Finally, he sells the Crest of Artorias, which is required to open the door to Darkroot Forest, a more dangerous section of Darkroot Garden.

In *Dark Souls III*, he acts as the blacksmith in Firelink Shrine. At the beginning he is unable to infuse weapons without the correspondent coals found through the game to expand his services. Once the player has found a coal, returning it to him will unlock new infusion options.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre has a west country accent, a region in the UK famous as the supposed birthplace of King Arthur. While it's likely a choice of actor, the fact remains he is one of the few with a true regional English accent. Notably, the west country is frequently depicted/stereotyped as the countryside in media. The line by Rickert, "an old smith out in the country", may allude to Andre.
Andre is one of the few characters that do not disintegrate when killed. This may be because he uses a unique model, or perhaps signifies he is not an Undead or monster.
It was originally intended that Andre was to be a descendant of Gwyn and that he would have a key role in the story, but this idea was scrapped.
Andre is one of the few characters in *Dark Souls* whose mouth moves when he speaks (the others being Quelaag's Sister, Kingseeker Frampt, Alvina and Darkstalker Kaathe).

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : **Andre of Astora** (アストラのアンドレイ) is a character in *Dark Souls*. He is a blacksmith that will likely prove invaluable to the player throughout the game. Andre is voiced by Sean Barrett, who also voiced Ingward and Petrus of Thorolund.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : Despite what common sense might dictate, Andre does not use his hammer to fight, preferring to simply use his bare hands. This certainly does not mean that he is a pushover, however; his heavier punches can knock players off their feet, while his jabs are fast and can quickly deal a lot of damage. Andre has a roster of moves unique to him, including a drop kick that has heavy knockback and deals high damage. He also sports unusually high health for a character of his stature, so it may take a while to wear him down.

title: Antiquated Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Antiquated Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - availability 
 availability : The Antiquated Set is obtainable after talking with Dusk of Oolacile. She first must be rescued from the Golden Crystal Golem behind the Hydra in Darkroot Basin.

The set will spawn on a corpse that appears at the far end of the lake, near where the Golden Golem spawns. If the set does not appear initially, quitting and reloading or exiting the area and re-entering can force it to spawn.

title: Antiquated Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Antiquated Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - lead 
 lead : The **Antiquated Set** is a light armor set in *Dark Souls*. The set is also worn by Dusk of Oolacile.

title: Antiquated Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Antiquated Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - upgraded_stats 
 upgraded_stats : The Crown of Dusk cannot be upgraded. For the other armor pieces, the maximum upgrade level is +5.

title: Antiquated Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Antiquated Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - plot 
 plot : The Antiquated Set was worn by female royalty in the realm of Oolacile. The set encountered in game belongs to Dusk of Oolacile, who eventually perished in the Darkroot Basin.

title: Antiquated Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Antiquated Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - notes 
 notes : Prior to patch 1.04/1.05, the Antiquated Skirt gave by far the best defense and resistance for its weight, although it still had no Poise. It was nerfed heavily with the patch.
The Crown of Dusk cannot be upgraded.

title: Antiquated Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Antiquated Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Antiquated Set is most notable for its headpiece, the Crown of Dusk, which increases magical damage dealt and taken. The set as a whole possesses very high Curse resistance, as well as magic defense, but is weak against all other types of damage overall.

title: Armor (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Armor (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - upgrading 
 upgrading : Like weapons, most but not all armor pieces can be upgraded. Armor can be upgraded to +10 or to +5 for those that require Twinkling Titanite. Armor cannot be upgraded down other upgrade paths. Upgraded armor yields higher defensive values and elemental resistance, but never alters Poise.

title: Armor (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Armor (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - armor_categories 
 armor_categories : Armor sets are divided into three categories based on their total weight:
Light Armor Sets (0 - 19.9)
Medium Armor Sets (20 - 39.9)
Heavy Armor Sets (40+)

Each armor set is divided into four pieces based on the body part protected:
Head Armor
Chest Armor
Hands Armor
Legs Armor
Most armor sets are complete, but there are some unique pieces of armor that are not part of a set, and other sets that do not have all four pieces.

title: Armor (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Armor (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - lead 
 lead : **Armor** is a type of equipment in *Dark Souls* that provides protection against both physical (regular, strike, slash, thrust) and elemental (magic, fire, lightning) damage. Armor also increases resistance against negative status effects and it can increase the player's poise (stagger resistance).

Every armor item has a weight. While equipped, the item's weight is added to the player's effective equipment load, which can slow the player's movement speed and stamina recovery.
